title: Surgical Mapping with Advanced 3D-Reconstruction in Minimally Invasive Liver Surgery
summary:
Liver surgery requires very careful preparation because the anatomy of the liver varies from person to person. In particular, the spatial relationships between the blood vessels and bile ducts running through the liver and the diseased area that needs to be removed are crucial for planning a liver operation. Therefore, before surgery, computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans are used to carefully plan which part of the liver will be removed and which blood vessels must be preserved.
Typically, these images are displayed on a screen as a series of two-dimensional (2D) slices. Based on these images, the treating surgeons must mentally reconstruct a three-dimensional representation of the liver in order to prepare for and subsequently perform the operation.
In this study, we aim to investigate whether an additional three-dimensional (3D) visualization of your liver may help improve surgical planning. For this purpose, computer-based spatial reconstructions are generated from the CT images that are already available from your routine medical examinations. These reconstructions allow the surgical team to better understand the relationships between important anatomical structures such as blood vessels, bile ducts, and the location of a tumor before the operation.
The aim of the study is to determine whether this additional 3D visualization can facilitate surgical planning and, for example, reduce the duration of the operation.
In addition to the potential impact of 3D-based surgical planning on operative time, the study will also assess possible effects on:
• blood loss during surgery
• the size of the resected diseased liver tissue compared to healthy liver tissue (impact of surgical planning on the remaining liver volume)
• the cost-effectiveness of using 3D reconstruction software
• changes in the mental and physical workload of the operating surgeon
conditions: Liver surgery, liver malignancies, surgical planning

interventions.name:
Intervention arm:
Advanced preoperative 3D-reconstruction of CT and/or MRI pictures for pre- and intraoperative surgical mapping and navigation.

Control arm:
Standard minimally invasive liver surgery with conventional 2D evaluation of CT and/or MRI data and intraoperative mapping and navigation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Indication for elective liver resection (benign or malignant disease)
2. Availability of contrast-enhanced preoperative CT and/or MRI suitable for 3D reconstruction
3. Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Emergency liver surgery
2. Liver transplantation or living donor hepatectomy
3. Previous major liver resection
4. Preoperative known necessity of further extrahepatic resections or extensive adhesolysis
5. Inability to provide informed consent
6. Current institutionalization on court or official order
7. Current or planned Pregnancy preoperatively
